summary: Free function that detects x86 CPU features via the CPUID instruction and returns a feature-flag bitmask. Runs CPUID leaf 0 to obtain the vendor string (EBX/EDX/ECX), leaf 1 to test the EDX MMX bit (0x800000), then the extended leaves 0x80000000/-2147483647 to probe extended-function availability and the EDX sign bit (3DNow-class). When the vendor string matches 'AuthenticAMD', sets two additional AMD-specific EDX bits (0x40000000 and 0x400000). Called by sub_5172A5.

operations.description: Initialize the two local string buffers via strcpy: v27 = 'UnknownVendr' (from aUnknownvendr at 0x005AFA10) and v26 = 'AuthenticAMD' (from aAuthenticamd at 0x005AFA00).
Execute CPUID leaf 0 (EAX=0); initialize result flag v28 to 1, then store the returned vendor string into v27: v27[0]=EBX, v27[1]=EDX, v27[2]=ECX.
Proceed only if the value returned in EAX from CPUID leaf 0 is non-zero (maximum supported leaf).
Execute CPUID leaf 1 (EAX=1); store EAX into v27[4] and accumulate feature flags into v28: v28 |= 2, and v28 |= 0x20 when EDX bit 23 (0x800000, MMX-class) is set.
Execute CPUID leaf 0x80000000 (EAX=0x80000000) to query the maximum extended function number.
Proceed if the extended maximum leaf exceeds 0x80000000; then set v28 |= 4, execute CPUID with EAX=-2147483647, and set v28 |= 0x80 when the returned EDX is negative (bit 31, 3DNow-class).
If memcmp(v26, v27, 0xC) == 0 (the CPUID vendor string equals 'AuthenticAMD'), set v28 |= 0x100 when EDX bit 30 (0x40000000) is set and return v28 | (EDX bit 22 (0x400000) ? 0x200 : 0).
Return the accumulated feature-flag bitmask v28.

clean_pseudocode: vendor[0] = ebx; vendor[4] = edx; vendor[8] = ecx;
unresolved: Precise meaning of each returned flag bit (0x02, 0x20, 0x04, 0x80, 0x100, 0x200) is inferred from standard CPUID feature semantics, not confirmed by runtime evidence.
The literal 0x800000 was resolved by the decompiler as the address unk_800000; semantically it is an EDX bitmask test (bit 23), not a real memory reference.
The vendor-string buffer v27 and AMD-detection string v26 relationship is clear, but why non-AMD CPUs return before setting the 0x100/0x200 bits is only inferred.
